title: Cohere Rerank 5 | More Relevant Context for RAG and Agents
html:
Introduction

Today, we're releasing Rerank 5, our most advanced enterprise retrieval models yet, available in Pro and Fast tiers.
Rerank 5 helps teams find the right information, send the most relevant context to their LLMs, and give customers more tailored search experiences. With Rerank 5 Pro, we’ve set a new standard in reranking quality, especially on reasoning-intensive search, visually rich documents, and key enterprise domains. Rerank 5 Fast brings that quality to latency- and cost-sensitive workloads. Both models introduce Context Focus, which pinpoints the most relevant spans of text within documents, going beyond document- or chunk-level retrieval to surface precisely the information that matters.
Every token your LLM reads is a token you pay for, and retrieval decides which tokens those are. As agents run more searches over longer documents, retrieval has become a key lever enterprises have over their AI cost, latency, and answer quality.
Rerank 5 joins Embed 5 and Parse 5 as part of our latest generation of search models. It is generally available today on the Cohere API and Model Vault, Microsoft Foundry, Amazon SageMaker, and to all North users. API pricing is $0.05 per 1M tokens for Pro and $0.02 for Fast.

Performance

Rerank 5 Pro leads public benchmarks such as ViDoRe V3, nanoMTEB, BRIGHT, and BEIR - outperforming every competing model tested. Of the 46 composite datasets evaluated, Rerank 5 Pro ranked first on 39 and placed at least second in 43. Models are evaluated using RCP-nDCG@10, a Cohere-developed methodology designed to address limitations in traditional nDCG caused by incomplete relevance judgments (qrel coverage).
The advantage is particularly pronounced on BRIGHT, a benchmark testing reasoning-intensive retrieval, where identifying relevant documents requires deeper understanding beyond keyword or semantic similarity. Rerank 5 Pro scores 82.2, outperforming Voyage AI Rerank 3 by 5.8 points and Rerank 4 Pro by 12.4 points, its largest generational gain across the four headline benchmarks. Pro also leads the strongest external competitor by 1.6 points on ViDoRe V3, 1.8 on BEIR, and 3.4 on nanoMTEB. These gains are increasingly important for agentic workflows, where complex, multi-step queries demand the ability to reason about relevance and return evidence that may not closely resemble the original query.
Rerank 5 Fast delivers substantial quality gains in the speed-optimized tier. In all four benchmarks, it outperforms Voyage AI Rerank 3 Lite and Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B, as well as the much larger Qwen3-Reranker-8B and previous-generation Rerank 4 Pro.

Domain-specific performance

Across specialized enterprise domains, Rerank 5 demonstrates consistent leadership. In finance and economics, Rerank 5 Pro leads competition on visual retrieval from financial documents (ViDoRe Finance), numerical reasoning over financial reports (FinQA), and complex economics questions (BRIGHT Economics). This is where its lead is largest, outperforming Voyage AI Rerank 3 by 9.6 points.
Similar results extend across healthcare, scientific research, and energy-focused retrieval, where benchmarks test the ability to surface relevant information from specialized scientific literature, biomedical research, and climate-related content. See the full list of results here.

Multilingual

Rerank 5 Pro improves on Rerank 4 Pro in every language we evaluated, with gains of at least two points in Spanish, French, German, Arabic and Korean. It ranks first on 14 of the 19 non-English languages in our internal evaluation suite, including all six of the priority business languages shown below.
Against the competition, Pro leads Voyage AI Rerank 3 in every one of these languages. Its widest margins are in Japanese (+2.7), French (+2.3) and Arabic (+2.3). Rerank 5 Fast outperforms Voyage AI Rerank 3 Lite across all six, by as much as 4.5 points in Arabic. See the full results across all 19 languages here.

Model Spanish French German Arabic Japanese Korean
Cohere Rerank 5 Pro 91.2 90.5 90.6 89.7 89.4 91.8
Cohere Rerank 5 Fast 88.6 88.6 88.6 86.5 86.8 89.9
Voyage AI Rerank 3 89.4 88.2 89.4 87.4 86.7 89.9
Cohere Rerank 4 Pro 88.6 88.1 88.6 87.5 89.3 89.8
Voyage AI Rerank 3 Lite 86.0 84.7 86.3 82.0 83.8 86.6
Qwen3-Reranker-8B 85.4 84.0 86.2 84.4 85.9 88.0
Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B 76.9 74.2 78.0 74.6 78.6 80.8


Multilingual. Reranking quality (RCP-nDCG@10) by language on our internal evaluation suite across six selected languages. The entire suite consists of 20 world languages and 74 datasets.

Parsed PDFs

On retrieval tasks involving content extracted from PDFs, an important capability for enterprise document search, Pro achieves the highest average score of 89.9 in the evaluated suite. This puts it ahead of Voyage AI Rerank 3 (88.4) and Rerank 4 Pro (88.3). Fast follows closely at 88.5, marginally outperforming both models.

Latency + Throughput

Rerank 5 Fast is built for volume. Under sustained load, Fast reranks about 187 standard-length documents (1,000 tokens) per second on an NVIDIA A100 GPU - delivering 2.9x the throughput of Pro.
Fast also delivers nearly 3x faster response times than Pro, making it ideal for latency-sensitive applications and agents that run many searches per task. Pro remains best suited for applications where ranking quality takes priority over speed.

Context Focus: unlock smarter token economics

As documents grow longer and AI agents retrieve information from more sources, the amount of context passed to LLMs continues to increase. Yet, often only a few sentences within each document are relevant to the query. Processing unnecessary content drives up token costs, increases latency and can introduce noise that reduces answer quality.
Context Focus, a new optional capability launching with Rerank 5, goes beyond identifying relevant documents to pinpoint the specific passages that matter most. Configurable thresholds let developers balance context reduction with evidence retention, while a single Rerank API call returns both document-level relevance scores and scored text spans. Applications can then pass only the most relevant evidence to an LLM, without adding steps to the retrieval pipeline.

Decouple context from answer quality

We measured how answer quality varied as Context Focus removes more of the retrieved text across 30 question-answering datasets. Removing half the context sacrificed only 2 percentage points of answer quality (96% retained), and removing three-quarters lost just 7 (87% answer quality retained). Context Focus therefore works like a dial: moderate settings are close to free, and teams that need bigger savings can trade some quality for up to 10x less context.


We then gave a search agent a retrieval stack built up one step at a time, starting from keyword search (BM25). Adding Rerank 5 Pro raised accuracy from 46% to 49%. Turning on Context Focus then cut tokens and raised accuracy further. At the default threshold (0.1), tokens per task fell by 19% and accuracy rose to 57%. At 0.4, tokens fell by 34%, lower on every dataset, and accuracy reached 58%. Altogether, the full stack with Context Focus at 0.4 used 35% fewer tokens than BM25 alone, at higher accuracy (58% vs 46%). On the six deep-search benchmarks, it used 41% fewer tokens, and accuracy rose from 39% to 52%, with every benchmark improving on both measures. ​

Calibrated relevance scores

With Rerank 5, a score of 0.7 now means a 70% chance the document is useful.
Every reranker returns a relevance score, but until now those scores were mostly good for sorting. What counted as a "good" score changed from model to model. Teams had to tune a cutoff for each model and re-tune it on every upgrade.
Rerank 5's scores are calibrated out of the box: the 

relevance_score
returned with each result reads as the probability that the document is useful, with no change to your request or the response format. Pro and Fast also agree on where the line is: "more likely useful than not" is a score of 0.50 for Pro and 0.45 for Fast.


We checked this against two independent sets of human judgments that no model was trained on: a blind panel of graders and NIST's TREC Deep Learning assessors. On both, Rerank 5 follows the diagonal far more closely than any other reranker. Competing models sit below it, overstating relevance: documents Voyage AI Rerank 3 scored around 0.55 were only 24% useful to the human graders.
The table below sums this up as expected calibration error (ECE): the average gap between a model's scores and the real share of useful documents, where 0 is perfect. Rerank 5's is about 0.06 on both sets of judgments; every other reranker we tested has nearly four times that error or more. Calibration doesn't cost ranking quality, either: Rerank 5 Pro and Fast rank first and second in average precision on both.

Expected Calibration Error Judge
Model Humans NIST
Cohere Rerank 5 Pro 0.058 0.057
Cohere Rerank 5 Fast 0.058 0.058
Cohere Rerank 4 Pro 0.384 0.309
Voyage AI Rerank 3 0.234 0.307
Voyage AI Rerank 3 Lite 0.226 0.325


Expected Calibration Error sums up each line in the charts above: the average distance of its dots from the diagonal, weighted by how many documents each dot represents. In other words, how far a model's scores are from the real share of useful documents. Lower is better; 0 is perfect.

Why it matters

  • Filter by relevance, not by count. Instead of passing a fixed top-k to your LLM, keep every document above the threshold. Narrow queries pass a few documents, broad ones pass more, and the model sees less noise.
  • Know when nothing relevant came back. If no document clears the threshold, an agent can rewrite the query or say it doesn't know, instead of answering from whatever ranked first.
  • One threshold across domains and model sizes. Across BRIGHT, NanoBEIR, and ViDoRe V3, the default stays between 0.47 and 0.53 for Pro, and Pro and Fast are within 0.05 of each other.

Start reranking

Rerank 5 Pro and Rerank 5 Fast are generally available through the Cohere API, Model Vault, Microsoft Foundry (Fast, Pro), and Amazon SageMaker (Fast, Pro), and to all North users. For private deployments in your own VPC or on-premises, speak to a member of our team.
Rerank 5 sits on top of the retrieval stack you already have. It works with any keyword, vector or hybrid search, with no re-indexing, and is available through frameworks including LangChain, Haystack, Elasticsearch and Weaviate. Read the documentation.
Start by creating an API key, then use the code snippets below to quickly make your first query.

      
#rerank with Context Focus
import os
import requests

query = "How much did card provisions rise in Q3?"

documents = [
    "Market update. Commercial real estate prices fell 6% this year as office "
    "vacancies climbed. Analysts expect refinancing pressure on landlords to "
    "persist into next year.",
    "Q3 credit quality. Net charge-offs held steady at 0.42% of average loans. "
    "Commercial real estate loans stood at $14.3 billion, or 9% of total loans. "
    "Office properties accounted for $2.1 billion of that balance. Card "
    "provisions rose $85 million on higher delinquencies.",
    "Q3 mortgage lending. Residential mortgage originations rose 11% as rates "
    "eased. The average loan-to-value ratio on new lending was 68%.",
]

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.cohere.com/v2/rerank",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CO_API_KEY']}"},
    json={
        "model": "rerank-v5.0-pro",
        "query": query,
        "documents": documents,
        "top_n": 2,
        "relevant_spans": {"mode": "enabled", "threshold": 0.4, "max_spans": 10}, #toggle Context Focus
    },
)
response.raise_for_status()

for result in response.json()["results"]:
    document = documents[result["index"]]
    print(f"{result['relevance_score']:.2f}  {document[:60]}...")
    for span in result.get("relevant_spans") or []:
        print(f"      {span['score']:.2f}  {document[span['start']:span['end']]}")

Last thoughts

Try Rerank 5 inside a full retrieval stack. Compass Cloud, our managed search and retrieval platform, brings parsing, embedding, hybrid search and Rerank together in one service, with Cohere managing the infrastructure. It's now in private beta for teams building retrieval-heavy and agentic applications. Request access.
Follow us on X and LinkedIn for the latest from Cohere, and email search@cohere.com with any other questions.

Rerank 5帮助团队找到正确的信息，将最相关的上下文发送给他们的LLM，并为客户提供更量身定制的搜索体验。借助 Rerank 5 Pro，我们在重新排名质量方面设立了新标准，特别是在推理密集型搜索、视觉丰富的文档和关键企业领域方面。 Rerank 5 Fast 为延迟和成本敏感的工作负载带来了这种质量。这两种模型都引入了上下文焦点，它可以精确定位文档中最相关的文本范围，超越文档或块级检索，精确地显示重要的信息。

表现

Rerank 5 Pro 领先ViDoRe V3 、 nanoMTEB 、 BRIGHT和BEIR等公共基准测试 - 优于所有测试的竞争模型。在评估的 46 个复合数据集中，Rerank 5 Pro 在 39 个数据集中排名第一，在 43 个数据集中至少排名第二。模型使用RCP-nDCG@10 进行评估，RCP-nDCG@10是 Cohere 开发的方法，旨在解决传统 nDCG 中因不完整的相关性判断（qrel 覆盖）而导致的局限性。
这一优势在 BRIGHT 上尤其明显，BRIGHT 是一种测试推理密集型检索的基准测试，其中识别相关文档需要对关键字或语义相似性之外的更深入的理解。 Rerank 5 Pro 得分为 82.2，比 Voyage AI Rerank 3 高出 5.8 分，比 Rerank 4 Pro 高出 12.4 分，这是四个主要基准测试中最大的代际收益。 Pro 在 ViDoRe V3 上领先最强大的外部竞争对手 1.6 分，在 BEIR 上领先 1.8 分，在 nanoMTEB 上领先 3.4 分。这些收益对于代理工作流程越来越重要，其中复杂的多步骤查询需要能够推理相关性并返回可能与原始查询不太相似的证据。
Rerank 5 Fast 在速度优化层中提供了显着的质量提升。在所有四个基准测试中，它的性能均优于 Voyage AI Rerank 3 Lite 和 Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B，以及更大的 Qwen3-Reranker-8B 和上一代 Rerank 4 Pro。

特定领域的性能

在专业企业领域，Rerank 5 展现了一致的领导力。在金融和经济学领域，Rerank 5 Pro 在金融文档视觉检索 (ViDoRe Finance)、财务报告数字推理 ( FinQA ) 和复杂经济学问题 (BRIGHT Economics) 方面处于领先地位。这是其领先优势最大的地方，比 Voyage AI Rerank 3 高出 9.6 个百分点。
类似的结果延伸到医疗保健、科学研究和以能源为中心的检索，其中基准测试从专业科学文献、生物医学研究和气候相关内容中显示相关信息的能力。请在此处查看完整的结果列表。

多种语言

在我们评估的每种语言中，Rerank 5 Pro 都比 Rerank 4 Pro 有所改进，西班牙语、法语、德语、阿拉伯语和韩语至少提高了两分。在我们的内部评估套件中，它在 19 种非英语语言中的 14 种中排名第一，其中包括如下所示的所有六种优先商业语言。
在竞争中，Pro 在每一种语言上都领先 Voyage AI Rerank 3。其差距最大的是日语（+2.7）、法语（+2.3）和阿拉伯语（+2.3）。在所有六种语言中，Rerank 5 Fast 的表现均优于 Voyage AI Rerank 3 Lite，高出 4.5 分（阿拉伯语）。 请在此处查看所有 19 种语言的完整结果。

已解析的 PDF

在涉及从 PDF 中提取内容的检索任务（企业文档搜索的一项重要功能）中，Pro 在评估套件中取得了最高平均分 89.9 分。这使其领先于 Voyage AI Rerank 3 (88.4) 和 Rerank 4 Pro (88.3)。 Fast 紧随其后，为 88.5，略微优于这两个模型。

延迟+吞吐量

Rerank 5 Fast 专为容量而设计。在持续负载下，Fast 在 NVIDIA A100 GPU 上每秒对约 187 个标准长度文档（1,000 个令牌）进行重新排序 - 吞吐量是 Pro 的 2.9 倍。
Fast 还提供比 Pro 快近 3 倍的响应时间，使其成为对延迟敏感的应用程序和每个任务运行多次搜索的代理的理想选择。 Pro 仍然最适合排名质量优先于速度的应用程序。

背景焦点：解锁更智能的代币经济

随着文档变得越来越长，AI 智能体从更多来源检索信息，传递给LLM的上下文数量不断增加。然而，每个文档中通常只有几个句子与查询相关。处理不必要的内容会增加令牌成本，增加延迟，并可能引入噪音，从而降低答案质量。
Context Focus 是随 Rerank 5 一起推出的一项新可选功能，它不仅可以识别相关文档，还可以查明最重要的特定段落。可配置的阈值让开发人员可以平衡上下文减少和证据保留，而单个 Rerank API 调用会返回文档级相关性分数和评分文本范围。然后，应用程序可以仅将最相关的证据传递给LLM，而无需在检索管道中添加步骤。

将上下文与答案质量分离

我们测量了当 Context Focus 在 30 个问答数据集中删除更多检索到的文本时，答案质量的变化情况。删除一半的上下文仅牺牲了 2 个百分点的答案质量（保留了 96%），删除四分之三的上下文仅损失了 7 个百分点（保留了 87% 的答案质量）。因此，Context Focus 的工作原理就像一个旋钮：适度的设置几乎是免费的，需要更多节省的团队可以用一些质量来换取最多 10 倍的上下文。


然后，我们为搜索代理提供了一个检索堆栈，从关键字搜索 (BM25) 开始，一步一步构建。添加 Rerank 5 Pro 将准确率从 46% 提高到 49%。打开上下文焦点然后削减标记并进一步提高准确性。在默认阈值 (0.1) 下，每个任务的令牌下降了 19%，准确率上升至 57%。在 0.4 时，令牌下降了 34%，每个数据集上的令牌都下降了，而准确率达到了 58%。总而言之，上下文焦点为 0.4 的完整堆栈使用的令牌比单独使用 BM25 少 35%，且准确度更高（58% vs 46%）。在六个深度搜索基准测试中，它使用的标记减少了 41%，准确度从 39% 上升到 52%，每个基准测试在这两项指标上都有所提高。 ​

校准的相关性分数

使用 Rerank 5，现在得分为 0.7 意味着该文档有 70% 的机会有用。
每个重新排名器都会返回一个相关性分数，但到目前为止，这些分数大多适合排序。不同模型的“好”分数的定义也不同。团队必须调整每个模型的截止值，并在每次升级时重新调整。
Rerank 5 的分数是开箱即用的：

relevance_score
每个结果返回的内容都是文档有用的概率，您的请求或响应格式没有变化。 Pro 和 Fast 也就界线达成一致：“更有可能有用”，Pro 的得分为 0.50，Fast 的得分为 0.45。


我们对照两组独立的人类判断进行了检查，没有对任何模型进行训练：盲评小组和 NIST 的 TREC 深度学习评估员。在这两个方面，Rerank 5 比任何其他重新排名器都更接近对角线。竞争模型位于其下方，夸大了相关性：Voyage AI Rerank 3 得分约为 0.55 的文档对人类评分者来说只有 24% 有用。
下表将其总结为预期校准误差 (ECE)：模型分数与有用文档的真实份额之间的平均差距，其中 0 是完美的。两组判断的 Rerank 5 约为 0.06；我们测试的所有其他重新排序器的错误率几乎是该错误的四倍或更多。校准也不会影响排名质量：Rerank 5 Pro 和 Fast 在平均精度方面分别排名第一和第二。

为什么这很重要

  • 按相关性过滤，而不是按计数过滤。不要将固定的 top-k 传递给你的LLM，而是让每个文档都高于阈值。窄查询传递一些文档，宽查询传递更多文档，并且模型看到的噪音更少。
  • 知道什么时候没有相关的信息返回。如果没有文档清除阈值，代理可以重写查询或说它不知道，而不是从排名第一的任何文档进行回答。
  • 跨领域和模型大小的一个阈值。在 BRIGHT、NanoBEIR 和 ViDoRe V3 中，Pro 的默认值保持在 0.47 到 0.53 之间，Pro 和 Fast 之间的差异在 0.05 以内。

首先创建 API 密钥，然后使用下面的代码片段快速进行第一个查询。

      
#rerank with Context Focus
import os
import requests

query = "How much did card provisions rise in Q3?"

documents = [
    "Market update. Commercial real estate prices fell 6% this year as office "
    "vacancies climbed. Analysts expect refinancing pressure on landlords to "
    "persist into next year.",
    "Q3 credit quality. Net charge-offs held steady at 0.42% of average loans. "
    "Commercial real estate loans stood at $14.3 billion, or 9% of total loans. "
    "Office properties accounted for $2.1 billion of that balance. Card "
    "provisions rose $85 million on higher delinquencies.",
    "Q3 mortgage lending. Residential mortgage originations rose 11% as rates "
    "eased. The average loan-to-value ratio on new lending was 68%.",
]

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.cohere.com/v2/rerank",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CO_API_KEY']}"},
    json={
        "model": "rerank-v5.0-pro",
        "query": query,
        "documents": documents,
        "top_n": 2,
        "relevant_spans": {"mode": "enabled", "threshold": 0.4, "max_spans": 10}, #toggle Context Focus
    },
)
response.raise_for_status()

for result in response.json()["results"]:
    document = documents[result["index"]]
    print(f"{result['relevance_score']:.2f}  {document[:60]}...")
    for span in result.get("relevant_spans") or []:
        print(f"      {span['score']:.2f}  {document[span['start']:span['end']]}")
